title: The known defect list has no element of its own in S4, and the two consumed rwb-document reads and the rwb-case answer publish no S4 contract row
source: _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4, two tables and five REST operations); Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.5.1, A2.5.2, A2.5.3.1, A2.5.3.3); Recovery Workbench FSD P5 Document hub v3 (A2.16, FEAT-DCM-16); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (feature row FEAT-LIT-05); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T3.1, T4, T5.2, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Feature List v4 (FEAT-DCM-16, FEAT-LIT-05); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-005, its Data and Endpoints tables)
section: APP s2 Business rationale; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3, 4 and 8; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.7 Tables owned; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan; s19 Out of scope; CON s2, s3, s7 AC2 and AC3, s11 Data, s12.2, s12.7, s12.8, s13
description: The legacy story tests the pack against a known defect list and names what is missing, and no S4 source defines that list: the FSD S4 A2.5 names it only in the rule text of R-LIT-16 to R-LIT-18, the TSD S4 holds no defect-list table and no defect-list field, and the ownership rows of S4 give the service two tables only, legal_action and hearing. The only checklist in the sources is FEAT-DCM-16 of module P5, the document checklist per case type held as reference data, and that feature states that it is the source the pack checks of Epics 4 and 5 read (R-LIT-16, R-LIT-17); the legacy story also lists FEAT-DCM-16 as a prerequisite. The stories therefore read the defect list as that checklist on the owner's operation GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist (API-P5-008), read the stored documents of the case on GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents (API-P5-002), read the case and answer the case move to rwb-case, and store no checklist row, no document row and no completeness flag of their own. The two P5 operations are published by RWB-P5-E1040-APP and RWB-P5-E1026-APP and no P5 contract story carries either as a baseline. None of the three consumed rows is in the plan: the contract-dependency row of both slices is None, so the stories build against the published documents and the fakes and the absence is recorded here instead of being turned into an invented C row.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack list two tables, hearing and legal_action, and five REST operations, none of which is a defect-list or checklist read; TSD S4 v2 T3.1 defines legal_action (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029) only; FSD S4 A2.5.3.1 gives VR-S4-005-1 and the rules R-LIT-18 and R-LIT-32 with no field, list or table for the defect list; FSD P5 A2.16 and the feature list row FEAT-DCM-16 describe the document checklist per case type as reference data and name the pack checks of Epics 4 and 5 as its consumers; RWB-P5-E1040-APP section 12 declares GET /cases/{caseId}/document-checklist as API-P5-008 and states that no document type or required flag is code; RWB-P5-E1026-APP section 12 declares GET /cases/{caseId}/documents as API-P5-002; TSD S4 v2 T5.2 names the published Java interfaces P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation, and T-A.1 lists five S4 operations only; the plan rows of RWB-S4-E5005-APP and RWB-S4-E5005-CON carry C as an empty list.
area: Contract and data, S4 rwb-litigation with P5 rwb-document and P3 rwb-case
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the P5 rwb-document owner and the P3 rwb-case owner
proposed: Keep the two metadata rows as the plan gives them, build against API-P5-008, API-P5-002 and the rwb-case answer with their fakes, and let step D1 decide whether the three consumed rows become C dependencies of this key or a baseline of RWB-P5-E1040-CON is raised.

title: The trigger of the check, the item state, the missing-item element and the activity name have no source, and the legacy key carries no requirement id in the plan
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (A2.5.2, A2.5.3.1, A2.5.4.4, Requirements served); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (heading RWB-E5-005, its Acceptance criteria and Test cases tables); _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (both slices of RWB-E5-005, the reqs list and the acs list); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-LIT-16 to R-LIT-18, R-LIT-31, R-LIT-32); Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2 (T-A.2, T4)
section: APP s1 Story; s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 1 and 2; s12.5 Workflows and activities; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan; s18 Traceability; CON s2, s3, s7 AC1 and AC2, s11 Data, s12.5, s12.8, s18
description: The legacy story says the check runs unattended and that its trigger is the arrival of the data and the rule version the feature needs, the FSD S4 A2.5.2 names the trigger as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and A2.5.4.4 declares no background event at all, so the trigger has no single source. Both stories read the trigger as the case stage that the parent CaseWorkflow forwards to the litigation child on task queue rwb-litigation, on the PACK_ASSEMBLY, PACK_DEFECT_HOLD and FILING_REJECTED stages, and declare no event and no Schedule, because DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key and the S4 IN row of Architecture v5 slide 19 lists no document event. The item state (present or missing), the missing-item element, the activity name checkPackDefects, the decision code and the case answer shape are design names with no source, so they are carried as this baseline's element names and marked with the placeholder. The requirement id is the same kind of absence in the other direction: the legacy story master carries no requirement, the plan's reqs list for both slices is empty, and the only sourced requirement is REQ-S4-002 of the FSD S4 Requirements served, which the two traceability sections cite.
evidence: FSD S4 v3 A2.5.2 gives the step row Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer, and A2.5.4.4 is the row None, No background event; the legacy story AC1 says the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place and When its trigger arrives, and its metadata row Depends on is FEAT-LIT-04, FEAT-DCM-16; TSD S4 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 carry no defect-check operation, no item state and no missing-item element, and T4 gives the LITIGATION state machine with no trigger for the pack check; the plan rows of both slices carry reqs as an empty list and the legacy index of RWB-E5-005 carries no requirement id; FSD S4 v3 Requirements served gives REQ-S4-002 for the assembled and checked pack.
owner_role: S4 rwb-litigation service owner with the solution architect
proposed: Start the step from the case stage the parent forwards, publish the item state and the missing-item element in the baseline review, and let step D1 confirm the trigger and the REQ-S4-002 trace for this key.
